title: Align the catch-up refusal with the draft: a response code, not an HTTP status
description:
Writing draft-atwood-mimi-catchup (bead mimid-1wgh.37.104.13) found that
mimid's wire format is not in protocol-07's idiom, and the draft chose
the idiom over the implementation.

## The divergence

mimid signals the out-of-window refusal (docs/design/mimi-catchup.md
§5.1) as HTTP 410 with an RFC 9457 problem document:

- crates/mimid-server/src/hub/catchup.rs: HubError::CatchUpOutOfWindow
- crates/mimid-server/src/http.rs: 410 Gone, "catch-up-out-of-window"
- crates/mimid-server/src/follower/notify.rs: fill_gap matches
  PeerError::Rejected { status: 410, .. }

The draft (§4.3, §4.5) defines instead:

    enum { success(0), outOfWindow(1), noSuchRoom(2), notEntitled(3),
           (255) } CatchUpResponseCode;

    struct {
      CatchUpResponseCode responseCode;
      UTF8String errorDescription;
      select (responseCode) {
        case success:
          uint64 highestSequence;
          CatchUpEntry entries<V>;
        case outOfWindow:
          uint64 oldestHeld;
      };
    } CatchUpResponse;

## Why the draft's form is right

1. It is protocol-07's own idiom. Every other endpoint answers with a
   response struct carrying a code and a select (UpdateResponseCode,
   KeyMaterialUserCode, SubmitMessageResponse). A proposal that invents
   a different error convention for one endpoint is a proposal with an
   extra argument to lose.
2. An HTTP 410 cannot be told apart from a 410 produced by something
   that is not the hub: a proxy, a gateway, a CDN. The refusal makes a
   follower record a permanent loss and tell its users history is
   missing, so a status an intermediary can produce incidentally is the
   wrong carrier. The draft says this in §4.5 and §9.4.

## The work

- mimi-protocol: add CatchUpResponseCode and fold highest_sequence and
  entries into the success arm. CatchUpResponse::decode keeps rejecting
  trailing bytes and over-long entry vectors.
- hub/catchup.rs: answer 200 with outOfWindow instead of erroring, and
  carry oldestHeld (fanout_window already reads it).
- follower: match the response code, not the status. Keep treating a
  transport error as retryable and never as outOfWindow (draft §4.5
  says a requester MUST NOT infer it from a transport error).
- noSuchRoom and notEntitled likewise become codes. Decide whether the
  HTTP status stays 200 for all of them; the draft does not say, and
  protocol-07's other endpoints answer 200 with a refusal code.
- The existing tests move with it: hub_catchup.rs (6),
  follower_catchup.rs (10), two_provider_catchup.rs (2). The
  two-provider test asserts a real 410 today and would assert the code.

Do this only if the draft's form is the one we are proposing. If Mark
decides the HTTP status is better after all, the draft changes instead
and this bead closes as wontfix -- but then §4.5's argument needs an
answer.
close_reason: Done in 40d54f4f. CatchUpResponse carries a CatchUpResponseCode (success/outOfWindow/notAuthorized/noSuchRoom) with a select, following UpdateRoomResponse's pattern; names from GroupInfoCode, success at 0 from the majority. The hub answers 200 with a code instead of erroring, HubError::CatchUpOutOfWindow and CatchUpNotEntitled are deleted, and the follower reads the code. 30 tests, including two hand-encoded wire fixtures for the new arms and one that an undefined code is refused.
